Before trusting it: reproduce the VEP plugin exactly at the variant position on stop_gained rows. Report how many rows move each way (frameshift: nmd -> escape; start-proximal: escape -> nmd).

tasks.title: PM2: gnomAD v4 coverage for absent sites
tasks.desc:
Why: a variant absent from gnomAD counts toward PM2 even at sites gnomAD barely sequenced, where absence means nothing (ClinGen SVI PM2 guidance).

To do: add a gnomAD v4 coverage resource (needs your OK for the download/build and where it lives) and give absent-but-uncovered sites their own status, with no PM2.

Source: TODO.md "1b. gnomAD coverage for PM2".

notes.text: Self-contained description (Mario: board informative)
Plan: find a per-position gnomAD v4.1 resource, propose resource + threshold to Mario, then download, build lookup, new status, tests, fixture.

Findings 2026-11-10:
- Our gnomAD v4.1 VCF (/references, joint sites) only has lines where gnomAD saw a variant, so it cannot tell coverage at absent positions.
- gnomAD v4.1 publishes "allele number at all callable sites": tsv/exomes/gnomad.exomes.v4.1.allele_number_all_sites.tsv.bgz (1.1 GB) and tsv/genomes/gnomad.genomes.v4.1.allele_number_all_sites.tsv.bgz (12 GB). Format: locus (chr:pos), AN (+ capture-region flags in exomes). No .tbi published: needs a conversion to chrom/pos/AN + index. Max AN seen: exomes 1,448,354, genomes 152,426.
- Alternative coverage files are older/larger (genomes v3.0.1 coverage 80.9 GB; exomes v4.0 4.1 GB). AN is the better fit: it is the AN gnomAD would report if the variant existed.
Waiting for Mario: location and AN threshold.

Mario 2026-11-10: location OK (/data_lab_PGP/resources/annotation/gnomad_an/v4.1/); asked for literature before choosing the threshold.
Literature (sources in chat): no general ClinGen SVI coverage cutoff (SVI gnomAD v4 note, Aug 2024, gives none). VCEPs: RUNX1, DICER1 absent with >=20x; ATM >30x. Cardiomyopathy VCEP (MYH7 v2.0): upper bound of 95% CI <= 0.00004, as allele counts per AN (<=1 in >=120,000 ...). gnomAD (Gudmundsson 2022): flags variants covered in <50% of individuals; check AN/coverage before trusting absence.
Derived (mine): MYH7 rule with 0 alleles -> 3/AN <= 0.00004 -> AN >= 75,000.
FACT: scoring.py:110-116 reads FAF_POPMAX_BS1 per row, but no code or the gene list provides it, so MCAF is always 0.0001/2.5 = 0.00004 for every gene; acmg.py:118 uses 0.0001 instead.

Decision (Mario 2026-11-10): absence counts for PM2 only if exomes+genomes site AN >= -ln(0.05)/pm2_absence_af = 74,894 for 4e-5 (Cardiomyopathy VCEP MYH7 rule with 0 alleles; matches gnomAD's <50%-of-genomes warning). Threshold is a param.
Implemented (uncommitted): src/tools/build_gnomad_an_bed.sh (download from Google mirror, BED of runs of equal AN, tabix; round-trip identical on 50k real positions per set); VEP --custom gnomADv4AN_exomes/_genomes (BED, overlap; verified locally in the VEP container: SNV one value, deletion one per deleted base, insertion both flanks, uncovered empty); population.py new status absent_low_an + GNOMAD_SITE_AN (min over positions, empty = 0); --pm2-absence-af / params.pm2_absence_af; both fields added to vep_required_fields; README.
Tests: 5 new in test_population_frequency.py (22/22); full suite passes in the annotation_tests env.
Running: BED build (exomes downloaded, genomes 12 GB pending). Then: cluster fixture, status counts, tell Module 3 about absent_low_an and GNOMAD_SITE_AN.

2026-11-18: gnomAD AN BEDs built (exomes 1.15 GB, genomes 16 GB; MANIFEST.txt with sha256). Exomes BED matched the source TSV at 60/60 sampled positions. First genomes attempt failed on a locale bug in the size check (fixed in build_gnomad_an_bed.sh).
Known limit (not fixed): VEP returns nothing for bases with no interval in a file, so a deletion partly outside a file's coverage gets the minimum of its covered bases only. At capture edges this can overstate AN a little.
Cluster check: synthetic fixture test_data/raw_vcfs/an_spliceai2_fixture.vcf.gz (9 variants) with expected values in an_spliceai2_fixture.expected.tsv: absent with high AN, AN 0, low-AN SNV/deletion/chrY, an insertion, a present control.
2026-11-18: genomes BED matched the source TSV at 574/574 positions (one every 5M), all 25 contigs present. Ready for the cluster fixture run.

A variant absent from gnomAD now gets PM2 only where gnomAD genotyped enough alleles: exomes+genomes site AN ≥ 74,894 (for the 4e-5 PM2 threshold). Below that it is the new status `absent_low_an`: no PM2, no rarity bonus. New column `GNOMAD_SITE_AN`.
- Checked on the cluster: fixture `an_spliceai2_fixture` (2026-11-23, commit 76478fd, clean): 9/9 synthetic variants match the expected AN and status; PM2 only on the 4 well-covered absences (AN 0, 34k chrY, 71k deletion and 73k SNV lose it). Local tests 457 passed.
- Committed 0562b5c (not pushed). Module 3 note: walkthrough/20261123_module3_site_an_and_spliceai2.md, with a draft DEC.
- To decide: file the DEC in carve-platform? Does Module 3 compute PM2 on its own (then it must apply the same rule)?

notes.text: Self-contained description (Mario: board informative)

Question: PRED-15: (a) fork UTRAnnotator into this repo and make it emit every uORF class deterministically, or (b) accept and document the instability? I recommend (a): the instability flips high_impact/other on real rows (6 of 1,780 shared rows), and a pinned in-repo copy also helps RP-01.
Mario chose (a): fork UTRAnnotator into this repo and make it emit every uORF class deterministically.

Done locally (uncommitted): this repo now has its own copy of the plugin, src/external/vep_plugins/UTRAnnotatorPGP.pm, which reports every uORF class of a variant in a fixed order. Each 5UTR_annotation entry says which class it belongs to, and UTRAnnotator_status grades every class.
- Checked: the plugin compiles in the VEP container and gives identical output under 8 Perl hash seeds; the old selection loop gave a different class across those seeds. All 51 Python test modules pass.
- Left: two cluster runs of a 34-variant fixture (the variants whose class differed between F2005_union and F1830_union_avi), then src/tools/compare_utr5_runs.py. Commands and pass criteria: walkthrough/20261110_utrannotator_deterministic_fork.md.

tasks.desc:

Source: TODO.md checklist step 6.

notes.text: Plan: sample about 2,000 sites the old SpliceAI cache left unscored (seeded, recorded), build a fixture VCF, hand over the launch command, then count how many get a score.

tasks.title: VEP: stop the run when a plugin fails to load
tasks.desc:
Why: without --safe, VEP only warns when a plugin fails to compile or load (Runner.pm:886-915 in the container) and goes on. That plugin's columns then disappear without an error; for UTRAnnotator, every row becomes UTRAnnotator_status=not_annotated.

Proposal: add --safe to the VEP call, or check after VEP that the CSQ header has every expected plugin field and fail the task if one is missing.

Done when: a run with a broken plugin fails, and a normal fixture run still passes. Needs one cluster fixture run.

notes.text: the safe flag could interfere with the normal annotation if there is any plugin not working (like mastermind)? if so, the maybe we should try to fix this first and select the columns we are really using

Plan: first answer Mario's note - list the plugins in the VEP call, find which ones warn or fail in recent runs (e.g. Mastermind), and which plugin columns downstream code actually reads. Then propose --safe vs a header check on the plugins we use.

Answer to the note (checked in the VEP 111 container source):
- --safe only stops the run when a plugin fails to compile/instantiate (Runner.pm:899,912,948). A plugin failing on single variants stays a warning with or without --safe (OutputFactory.pm:2133), so --safe would not break normal runs that way.
- Side effect: with --safe, missing SIFT/PolyPhen in the cache are silently disabled instead of stopping VEP (Cache/Transcript.pm:161).
- Today's VEP task (2026-11-10 15:59) has columns from all 12 plugins, Mastermind included; stderr only container INFO lines.
- Not read anywhere (pipeline or Module 3 code): Mastermind, LoFtool, SpliceRegion.
Proposal: no --safe; after VEP, check the header has the columns of each plugin we read and stop with the plugin's name if one is missing. Removing unused plugins = separate task. Waiting for Mario's OK.
Question: Header check instead of --safe, and a separate task to drop Mastermind/LoFtool/SpliceRegion (+ unused SIFT/PolyPhen)?
Mario 2026-11-10: use BOTH --safe and the post-VEP column check (the SIFT/PolyPhen cache case is very rare and we do not read them).

Implemented (uncommitted): modules/local/vep.nf adds --safe and, after VEP, checks the CSQ header for params.vep_required_fields (nextflow.config, 15 "source:field" pairs: plugins and --custom sources read downstream). Missing field -> task fails naming the source.
Local checks: check logic on today's real VEP header -> OK; same header with am_pathogenicity and ReMM removed -> fails naming both; nextflow config parses; VEP-related tests 15/15 pass.
Pending cluster: (1) normal fixture passes; (2) run with --vep_alphamissense pointing to a missing file must fail in VEP_ANNOTATE ("Failed to instantiate plugin AlphaMissense").

Cluster 2026-11-10 sf05_safe_broken (missing AlphaMissense file): VEP_ANNOTATE failed in every chunk with 'Failed to instantiate plugin AlphaMissense: ERROR: Data file ... not found' (Runner.pm:912), run aborted, no table. 7 chunks x 6 attempts (errorStrategy retry, maxRetries 5), ~15 s each: retries are wasted but cheap, left as is. Pending: normal fixture sf05_safe_ok.

A VEP plugin that fails to load now stops the run, instead of silently dropping its columns.
- `--safe` on the VEP call: a plugin that cannot load fails VEP_ANNOTATE with VEP's own message.
- After VEP, the CSQ header must contain the 15 fields we read (plugins + --custom ClinVar/gnomAD/ReMM/SpliceVarDB), listed once in `vep_required_fields` (nextflow.config). A missing one fails the task naming source:field.

- cluster sf05_safe_ok (normal fixture): 37/37 tasks OK, VEP passed the check.
